This is a hands-on and operationally focused role, responsible for providing high-quality end-user support to Terex employees globally and ensuring consistent, reliable access to Terex IT services and tools. The Senior IT Service Desk Analyst plays a key role in ensuring stable, secure, and productive end-user experiences across the enterprise, providing advanced troubleshooting and acting as an escalation point for complex incidents. The role operates within a globally integrated, follow-the-sun support model, partnering closely with Desktop Side Support team, Desktop Engineering, Infrastructure, Security, and Application teams across regions. Key Responsibilities End User Support & Service Desk Operations Provide day-to-day support for Terex IT users globally across the Terex IT environment (hardware, operating systems, applications, and collaboration tools). Log, categorize, prioritize, and resolve incidents and service requests in line with defined SLAs and operational procedures. Troubleshoot and resolve complex end-user issues across Windows endpoints, identity/access, printing, network connectivity, and business applications; escalate effectively when needed. Execute routine service desk activities including user onboarding/offboarding support, password and access assistance, device setup guidance, and knowledge-driven request fulfillment. Incident Management & Advanced Troubleshooting Perform structured triage using available monitoring, logs, and diagnostic tools including Nexthink DEX solution; identify trends and recurring issues impacting user productivity. Act as an escalation point for complex incidents, driving thorough troubleshooting, coordination, and restoration of service. Collaborate with Desktop Side Support, Desktop Engineering, Infrastructure, Network, Security, and Application teams to drive resolution of cross-domain incidents. Communicate clearly with end users and stakeholders, providing timely updates, setting expectations, and confirming resolution and user satisfaction. Service Requests, Access & Device Support Fulfil service requests including software access, account support, and standard device troubleshooting using documented procedures and automation where available. Support identity and access requests (e.g. account access issues, MFA guidance, group membership changes) in line with security policies and approvals. Provide support for collaboration and productivity tooling (e.g. email, MS Teams, O365) and common peripherals (docking, printers, headsets). Support device lifecycle activities by coordinating with Desktop Side Support team (imaging, replacements, break/fix), and ensuring accurate asset and ticket records. Problem Management, Knowledge & Change Enablement Identify recurring incidents and contribute to problem management by capturing symptoms, workarounds, and supporting root cause investigations. Create and maintain knowledge articles, troubleshooting guides, and standard operating procedures to improve first-contact resolution. Support change implementation activities (communications, validation, hypercare) and ensure service desk readiness for new or changed services. Ensure accurate ticket documentation, categorization, and reporting inputs to support service performance, auditability, and continuous improvement. Operational Excellence & Documentation Maintain and improve service desk knowledge, scripts, and runbooks to standardize support and reduce time to resolve. Monitor queue health and support performance against SLAs; highlight risks, backlogs, and service-impacting trends. Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, including reducing repeat contacts, improving self-service, and standardizing support processes. Participate in on-call or follow-the-sun operational support rotations as required, providing mentoring and guidance to junior analysts when needed. Experience Required Qualifications 5–8 years of overall IT service desk / end-user support experience in an enterprise environment. Proven experience supporting end users across a broad range of workplace technologies (Windows endpoints, collaboration, identity/access, and business applications). Strong operational discipline with experience in incident, request, and problem management within an ITSM framework. Technical Skills Strong hands-on experience delivering service desk support with a customer-first approach. Strong troubleshooting skills across Windows OS, endpoint performance, printers/peripherals, and basic network connectivity (DNS, VPN, Wi-Fi, proxy). Experience supporting identity and access services (e.g., SSO, MFA), and common productivity/collaboration platforms used across the enterprise. Working knowledge of endpoint management concepts (device compliance, software deployment, remote support) and ability to partner with EUC/desktop engineering teams. Ability to document troubleshooting steps, resolution notes, and knowledge articles to improve support repeatability and first-contact resolution. Proven experience working within ITSM processes, including incident and request management, major incident support, and contributing to RCA and problem records. Education Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting a large-scale or global user base in a follow-the-sun support model. Exposure to security and compliance requirements for end-user support (access controls, data handling, endpoint protection). Experience supporting major incidents, coordinating with resolver groups, and communicating effectively with business stakeholders. Familiarity with ITIL-based operational processes and service management tooling. Certifications such as ITIL Foundation, Microsoft 365, or endpoint/support-related certifications. review_candidates.description: IT Support Analyst Our client is hiring an IT Support Analyst to provide first-level technical support to customers across a range of industries and IT environments. You’ll be the first point of contact for Windows, Microsoft 365, connectivity, and workstation issues. You’ll own tickets through resolution or escalation and keep customers informed along the way. This role is a good fit for someone with at least two years of IT support experience who enjoys working directly with customers and wants to build their troubleshooting and Microsoft 365 administration skills. You’ll work alongside experienced IT professionals and have access to ongoing training, mentorship, and opportunities to earn industry certifications. What you’ll do Provide first-level support by phone, chat, email, and service ticket. Prioritize requests and respond within established service level agreements. Troubleshoot Windows 10 and 11, Outlook, Teams, VPN connections, printers, network connectivity, and common business applications. Install, configure, and maintain workstations, software, and peripherals. Manage user accounts, security groups, access permissions, and multifactor authentication across Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, and Microsoft 365. Support Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online and SharePoint Online. Own assigned tickets through resolution or escalation. Keep customers updated and document troubleshooting steps, findings, and resolutions so advanced support teams can pick up where you left off. Help customers use their technology effectively and prevent recurring issues. What you’ll bring At least two years of professional IT technical support experience in a business environment. Hands-on experience troubleshooting Windows desktops, Microsoft applications, and common hardware and software issues. Working knowledge of Windows Server 2022 and 2025, Microsoft 365 administration, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Active Directory, and Microsoft Entra ID. Familiarity with multifactor authentication, user accounts, security groups, access permissions, PC hardware, basic networking, printers, and peripherals. Strong customer service skills and the ability to communicate clearly with both technical and nontechnical users. Ability to prioritize multiple support requests, meet response deadlines, and maintain clear ticket documentation. A dependable, collaborative approach and a willingness to take ownership of customer issues and learn from teammates. Authorization to work in the United States, a valid driver’s license, and reliable transportation. Ability to lift and move IT equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.
